current_content_summary: The absolute bottom of the theory stack (part of the 'prelude', compiled in with `-boot`, not requirable normally). Declares the primitive types unit (with tt), bool (with true/false and the core boolean connectives ! || \/ && /\ => <=>), polymorphic equality (=)/(<>), int, real, 'a distr (with mu : 'a distr -> ('a -> bool) -> real as the primitive probability-measure operator that Distr.ec's whole API is later built on), the universal witness : 'a value (EasyCrypt requires every type to be inhabited), and exn (exceptions).
version_diffs_found: None found by name in the scanned changelog window; this file is about as low-churn as EasyCrypt gets.
import_repair_note: NEVER add `require import Pervasive.` to repair a file. The engine exports Pervasive into every scope before it reads a line: src/ecCoreLib.ml defines `i_Pervasive = "Pervasive"` and src/ecCommands.ml (~line 876) exports it unconditionally at scope creation. `unit`, `bool`, `int`, `real`, `=`, `[!]`, `/\`, `=>` and the rest are always in scope. So a missing-symbol error naming one of them is never a missing Pervasive require -- it is shadowing, a `clone` whose path is wrong, or a genuinely different name. Emitting 'you must require Pervasive' is actively wrong advice, and proof_corpus/scripts/build_ec_migrations.py enforces that as ENGINE_PRELOADED so no generated rule can produce it. Pervasive has had no symbol removed in the tracked window.
